leftEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
leftEvidence.title: The written record removed and nailed to the cross

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Death in trespasses is followed by being made alive, forgiveness, removal of the written record, nailing it to the cross, and disarming rulers and authorities.
points.right: Gentiles and Israel, uncircumcision and circumcision, far and near, two and one remain named throughout.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.
points.right: The cross is not isolated from the passage’s concrete division between named peoples and their new shared access.

payload.posture: The two passages describe different obstacles removed in relation to the cross.

rightEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
rightEvidence.title: One body reconciled through the cross

payload.tension: Colossians names trespasses, a written record, rulers, and triumph; Ephesians names divided peoples, law, hostility, one body, and access.
payload.title: Record removed / hostility killed
